name: Aprosencephaly/Atelencephaly Spectrum

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Aprosencephaly/Atelencephaly Spectrum

criteria.description: Complete or near-complete absence of the forebrain (prosencephalon) on neuroimaging
Presence of midline craniofacial anomalies such as cyclopia, proboscis, or hypotelorism
Absence or severe hypoplasia of lateral and third ventricles on imaging
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with forebrain development (e.g., SHH pathway genes)
Prenatal ultrasound showing absent or abnormal forebrain structures

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of absence or near-absence of the forebrain on neuroimaging plus at least one major craniofacial anomaly
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on neuroimaging and clinical features; genetic testing can support but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe midline craniofacial malformations (e.g., cyclopia, proboscis)
searchTerms: severe facial midline defects like single eye

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absence of lateral and third ventricles
searchTerms: no lateral and third brain ventricles

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; no specific laboratory biomarkers identified
imaging: MRI or CT showing absence or severe hypoplasia of the forebrain
Midline craniofacial abnormalities visible on prenatal ultrasound or postnatal imaging
genetic: Pathogenic variants in SHH, ZIC2, SIX3, or other genes involved in forebrain development
other: Prenatal ultrasound findings suggestive of severe forebrain malformation

distinguishingFeatures: Partial fusion of cerebral hemispheres rather than complete absence
Variable severity of midline facial anomalies
Destruction of cerebral hemispheres with preserved falx cerebri
Presence of cerebrospinal fluid replacing brain tissue
No primary developmental absence of forebrain

redFlags: Severe midline craniofacial malformations at birth
Absence of cerebral hemispheres on neuroimaging
Failure to achieve developmental milestones if survival beyond neonatal period
references: Muenke M, Beachy PA. Holoprosencephaly. In: GeneReviews® [Internet]. University of Washington, Seattle; 2020.
Kawasaki K, et al. Aprosencephaly: Clinical and Radiological Features. J Neurol Sci. 2019.
